short_description: Consumer-facing nutrition trait that reports a cautious panel-relative signal for water-intake tendency within the current local reference panel.
summary_note: Usable consumer-facing nutrition trait with workable raw-array support and a clearer interpretation boundary between inherited water-intake tendency and real-world hydration habits for the no-imputation workflow.
what_it_measures: A panel-relative polygenic signal associated with a tendency toward higher or lower water intake, calibrated within the current local empirical reference panel.
interpretation_template: Water intake is presented here as a cautious relative nutrition signal, not a direct readout of how much water you currently drink each day. {interpretation}
caution_text: Use as a cautious panel-relative signal only. No imputation or ancestry-adjusted normalization is used, and the output should not be treated as a deterministic real-world result, a direct readout of current hydration behavior, or medical advice.
limitations: Percentiles and z-scores are relative to the local reference panel, not to a population-wide benchmark.
Real-world water intake depends strongly on climate, physical activity, body size, diet, salt intake, work routine, fasting, illness, and personal habit.
This trait should not be treated as a hydration assessment, kidney-health signal, or medical guidance.
confidence_note: Confidence reflects overlap and reference robustness under the no-imputation raw-array workflow, not certainty about the real-world trait.
reference_note: Percentiles and z-scores are calibrated against a local empirical reference artifact built from raw-array files in this project; they are panel-relative, not population-wide.
